title: Research a topic and write a short cited summary
outcome: A one-to-two page summary of a topic, based on credible sources, with correct in-text citations and a bibliography.

estimated_duration.label: About 3–4 hours across one or two sittings

prerequisites: A computer with a word processor (Word, LibreOffice or Google Docs)
required_inputs: The citation style you must use

steps.title: Frame the question
steps.instructions: Write your research question in one sentence and list 3–5 key terms with synonyms.
steps.check: Could someone else search using only your terms?

steps.title: Set up your library
steps.purpose: Capture sources correctly from the start.
steps.instructions: Install Zotero and its word-processor plugin; create a collection named after your topic.
steps.expected_output: An empty collection ready to fill.
steps.check: The plugin appears in your word processor.
steps.fallback: If you can't install software, keep a table of author, year, title, publication and link, and format citations by hand.

steps.title: Search and screen
steps.instructions: Search Google Scholar, filter to recent years and read abstracts. Use 'Cited by' on the strongest paper to find newer work.
steps.check: Each source directly addresses your question.
steps.warning: Being listed in a search engine does not make a source credible; check where it was published.

steps.title: Save sources
steps.instructions: Save each source to your Zotero collection and fix any missing or wrong details.
steps.check: Every item has author, year, title and publication.

steps.title: Read and note
steps.instructions: Read each source (or at least its introduction and conclusion) and write two or three bullet notes in your own words.
steps.check: Your notes are not copied sentences.
steps.fallback: If full text is behind a paywall, try the 'All versions' link or ask your library.

steps.title: Write with citations
steps.instructions: Write the summary from your notes and insert citations with the Zotero plugin as you go, then generate the bibliography in the required style.
steps.expected_output: A draft summary with citations and bibliography.
steps.check: Every claim from a source has a citation.

verification: Open three citations at random and confirm each leads to the source and supports the sentence it is attached to; confirm every in-text citation appears in the bibliography and the style matches your brief.
total_cost_notes: Both tools can be used without paying. Some full-text articles may need a subscription or library access; Zotero's free file storage is 300 MB.
accessibility_notes: Zotero's word-processor plugins add citations through menus, so you can work with the keyboard; check with your screen reader before a deadline.
low_bandwidth_notes: Read abstracts first and download full texts only for sources you will actually use.
success_criteria: The summary answers the research question.
At least five credible sources are cited.
Citations and bibliography follow the required style.
common_failure_modes: Starting to write before narrowing the question

troubleshooting.problem: The citation plugin doesn't appear in my word processor.
troubleshooting.fix: Restart the word processor after installing Zotero and check the Zotero documentation's word-processor section.
Add a more specific term, put exact phrases in quotation marks and filter by year.

example.input: Question: 'How does mobile money affect small businesses?'
example.output: A 600-word summary citing six studies, with a bibliography in the required style.

editorial.author: V2 research pass (AI-assisted, Claude)
